recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is needed for FHIR-27840; any future change to OperationOutcome success semantics should be handled as a new substantive tracker or through the already-audited FHIR-39622 family.
issue_request: FHIR-27840 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 after asking whether OperationOutcome.issue.severity information and OperationOutcome.issue.code informational could be used when an OperationOutcome reports successful checks or outcomes without actual issues. The accepted resolution required a usage note on OperationOutcome.issue.code explaining that codes should generally align with severity while preserving flexibility; it did not add a success message/code at that time.
initial_application: Commit 4f468df0510a78f38b65a3d8ec63b3f453d476c1 added the approved OperationOutcome.issue.code comment to source/operationoutcome/structuredefinition-OperationOutcome.xml. The current source still contains that comment, and source/fhir.ini confirms OperationOutcome is active in the current build.
additional_context: FHIR-32445 later reused OperationOutcome issue-severity for AuditEvent outcome and noted that issue-severity would be sufficient if a success code were added. FHIR-39622 then added success to issue-severity and recorded that it was not excluded from OperationOutcome; that later issue is already represented on the combined branch. This later success-code state explains current source and does not make FHIR-27840 incomplete.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The exact approved guidance is already present in the authoritative OperationOutcome StructureDefinition, and changing the current success-code state would revisit later published terminology decisions rather than reconcile FHIR-27840.

related_jiras.note: AuditEvent outcome terminology decision that expected reuse of issue-severity and discussed success-code sufficiency. It is separate from the seed and already represented on the combined branch.
